summary: Dedicated pool throughput fade and periodic p99 bursts during customer rollout — short-stream shadowing
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LuminOS observed repeated throughput degradation and p99 latency spikes in their dedicated GPU pool during a staged model rollout. The effect began ~2026-03-10 09:20 PDT and recurred during subsequent rollout windows. Impact: customer-facing API p99 increased from ~420ms to >3s and effective throughput fell ~40% for 5-10 minute windows.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (reserved) assigned to LuminOS, region us-west-2, mixed GPU type (A100+H100), pinned model redwood/longform-13b for rollout.

Observed behavior:
- Periodic (clustered) 5–12 minute intervals where p99 spikes and throughput drops.
- Spike windows correlated with a high rate of short-lived inference streams (<250ms) from a different tenant sharing the same pool.
- Autoscaler did not provision additional slots during the earliest minutes of the window; autoscale metrics showed allocation attempts but low successful GPU attachments.

Initial hypothesis:
- Short, high-frequency streams from another tenant were fragmenting batch slots and causing the scheduler to compact many small batches, increasing kernel overhead and creating slot starvation. The autoscaler telemetry appearing delayed/masked by heartbeat noise led to undersizing during the first minutes of each surge.

Steps to reproduce (attempted by Support/Eng):
1) Recreate a small-stream flood in a synthetic testbed attached to a dedicated pool with mixed short and long streams.
2) Start a rollout on a pinned model to simulate LuminOS traffic mix.
3) Observe scheduling logs, batch sizes, slot allocation, and autoscaler decisions (30m window).
steps_to_reproduce: Provision test dedicated pool in us-west-2 with mixed short (<250ms) and long (>2s) stream traffic pattern.
Simulate a burst of short lived streams at 200–400 rps from a shadow tenant for 8–12 minutes.
Run steady long-stream traffic (LuminOS-like) concurrently at 40–60 rps and start rolling model update.
Collect scheduler/batcher traces, autoscaler attach logs, and GPU slot allocation metrics for the window.
logs: 2026-03-10T09:26:12Z scheduler: observed 700 short_stream_starts in 60s from tenant=shadow-9
comments: 2026-03-10 10:05 - Support (Aisha): Logged with SRE + Customer. Collected traces and requested SRE to run targeted synthetic test; provided customer a temporary traffic-shaping workaround to reduce short stream concurrency.

2026-03-10 11:12 - SRE (Diego): Reproduced with local testbed. Observed slot fragmentation and delayed attach_failures tied to NVML timeout on mixed GPU nodes. Short streams occupied slot headers causing preemption of batched work.

2026-03-10 11:50 - SRE (Diego): Pushed a hotfix to scheduler to prefer coalescing small streams into ephemeral micro-batches and increased autoscaler polling frequency for affected pool. Monitoring will track p99/successful_attach for 24h.
2026-03-11 09:33 - Customer (LuminOS, S. Park): Confirmed that p99 spikes reduced at next rollout window. Noted one residual 2-minute spike; asked for root cause details and long-term mitigations.
investigation_notes: Testbed reproduction: synthetic short-stream flood reproduced throughput fade and p99 spikes within 4–6 minutes.

Root cause chain:
  1) High rate of short-lived streams (shadow tenant) created many small batches and frequent context switches.
  2) Scheduler assigned slot headers for each short stream; this fragmented GPU slot scheduling and reduced batch efficiency.
  3) NVML attach timeouts on mixed GPU nodes (A100+H100) caused transient attach failures, reducing usable slot capacity.
  4) Autoscaler telemetry aggregation window (30s default) smoothed the early signal; autoscaler did not request needed slot capacity until after visible throughput drop.
Telemetry artifacts: autoscaler_emit_delay_ms spiked to 1200ms during event; attach_fail_rate rose to 7% vs baseline 0.2%.
Model sensitivity: redwood/longform-13b long-context KV cache growth amplified memory pressure during the windows, exacerbating attach failures on heterogeneous nodes.
resolution_notes: Implemented a 2-stage mitigation: (1) short-term — applied traffic-shaping guidance to LuminOS (throttle concurrent short streams) and enabled the scheduler hotfix to micro-batch short streams; (2) medium-term — increased autoscaler polling frequency from 30s -> 8s for affected dedicated pools and added attach retry backoff jitter. Hotfix was rolled to us-west-2 at 2026-03-10T11:44Z. Post-change monitoring showed p99 returned to baseline (~420ms) and throughput recovered to >92% of steady-state within 6 minutes of each test window.
follow_up_actions: ENG-OPS: Create a scheduler improvement ticket to add explicit slot compaction heuristics for mixed short/long stream workloads (INT-6420).
INFRA: Validate NVML timeouts across heterogeneous GPU mixes and provide driver-level mitigation (upgrade plan for H100 nodes).
PRODUCT: Document 'short-stream guidance' for Dedicated customers and add auto-detect rule in Console to recommend traffic shaping when small-stream percentage >40%.
SRE: Reduce autoscaler default aggregation window for dedicated pools with mixed workloads and add synthetic short-stream canary to alert earlier.
estimated_customer_impact: LuminOS reported increased error-budget burn during rollout windows but no SLA breach; customer-facing endpoints experienced 5–10 minute degradation windows with p99 >3s.
